title: Denmark – Construction work – Løvbakkernes Vandværk
description: Ordregiver udbyder en totalentreprisekontrakt vedrørende projektering, opførelse og idriftsættelse af Løvbak-kernes Vandværk nord for Herning. Vandværk placeres på matrikel nr. 1r, Gullestrup, Herning Jorder. Det nye vandværk skal have en produktionskapacitet på 3 millioner m³/år, med mulighed for udvidelse til 4,5 millioner m³/år efter 2040. Hovedformålet med det nye vandværk er at sikre fremtidens produktion af drikkevand og højne Herning Vands forsyningssikkerhed. Desuden ønskes muligheden for at kunne udvide vandværket på sigt og sikre fleksibilitet i forhold til den fremtidige efterspørgsel på rent vand. Det nye vandværk ved Løvbakkerne omfatter blandt andet byggemodning, vandværksbygning, el- og maskinan-læg, håndtering af skyllevand og overfladevand, vejanlæg og udenomsarealer på vandværksgrundens matrikel. Visionen hos ordregiver er, at vandværket opføres på en måde, hvor det integreres harmonisk og naturligt i land-skabet. Samtidig ønskes placeringen tæt på forsyningens boringer og eksisterende læringsmiljøer udnyttet, så vandværkets udearealer bliver centrum for et nyt læringsrum med fokus på bæredygtig vandforvaltning, grund-vandsbeskyttelse og formidling om vand. Det nye vandværk forventes færdigt medio 2029.

title: Contrôle Montage FO 2027-2028 - lignes aériennes et pylônes
description:
Le présent appel d’offres porte sur la réalisation de contrôles de montage dans le cadre du remplacement de câbles de garde existants par des câbles OPGW 144 FO sur différentes lignes aériennes à haute tension de Swissgrid.


Le marché est divisé en deux lots :


  • Lot 1 – Suisse alémanique,Tessin : contrôles de montage dans le cadre des projets TR1011, TR1270 et TR1930, représentant au total 361 pylônes et environ 125 km de lignes.
  • Lot 2 – Suisse romande : contrôles de montage dans le cadre des projets TR1570, TR1600 et TR1602, représentant au total 319 pylônes et environ 104 km de lignes.


Les prestations comprennent notamment le contrôle des fixations des câbles de garde, des ponts et des descentes des câbles de garde, des amortisseurs de vibrations et des balises, ainsi que le contrôle de la flèche des câbles de garde. Selon le projet, elles comprennent également le contrôle des systèmes Latchway, des dispositifs ou boulons d’ascension ainsi que d’autres adaptations réalisées sur les installations des lignes aériennes. Les contrôles de montage effectués doivent être documentés conformément aux procès-verbaux de contrôle prescrits.


L’étendue détaillée des prestations ainsi que les exigences et quantités spécifiques à chaque projet sont définies dans les documents d’appel d’offres.

title: Strømavtale for innkjøp og videreformidling av kraft
description: 1 Oppdraget 1.1 Om oppdragsgiveren Ål Kraftverk KF, heretter kalt oppdragsgiveren, innbyr til konkurranse om innkjøp av tjenester om innkjøp og formidling av kraft til Ål Kraftverk KFs kunder. Ål Kraftverk KF er et heleid kommunalt foretak som er eid av Ål kommune. Foretaket ble opprettet i 1914 og forvalter de kommunale kraftrettighetene for Ål kommune og drifter Ylifossen kraftverk. De kommunale kraftrettighetene består av ca. 101 GWh konsesjonskraft, 80 GWh Erstatningskraft og andelskraft fra Usta og Nest Kraftverk på 45-65 GWh. Kraftverket har også produksjon fra Ylifossen kraftverk på ca. 12 GWh og andel i Lya kravferk på 30 prosent som utgjør ca. 5. GWh. Kommunen får finansielt oppgjør per kvartal av inntekter og kostander fra Lya fra Hafslund Eco. Til sammen utgjør dette rettigheter og produksjon for kommunen på ca. 250 GWh. Foretaket har konsesjon for salg innen Ål kommune sine grenser og kjøper tjenester for om lag 3500 kunder. Foretakets kunder hadde behov for ca. 81,3 GWh i 2025. 1.2 Omfanget av oppdraget Denne anskaffelsen innebærer en avtale om en tjeneste i form av innkjøp og videreformidling av kraft til Ål kraftverk KFs sluttbrukerkunder. Foretaket tilbyr en rekke ulike produkter til næringskunder, innbyggere, fritidsboliger og til kommunalt forbruk. Tjenesten leverandøren skal utføre for Ål Kraftverk KF er å kjøpe inn kraft for å dekke behovet til Ål kraftverk KFs sluttbrukerkunder for de ulike produktene kraftverket tilbyr. Kommunen vil dekke avviket mellom tilbyderens utgifter til kjøp av kraft i spotmarkedet på NordPool og inntektene fra detaljsalg til kunder av Ål Kraftverk KF. Kommunen betaler – for sitt forbruk – i dag en fastpris for kraft på 15 øre/KWh, men dette er foreslått endret til 20 øre/KWh for å gjenspeile selvkosten for kraften. For de øvrige kunder tilbys følgende produkter: Spotpris Fleksikraft på 1. 2. eller 3 år . - Inntil 80 % av fjorårets forbruk til fastpris og forbruket over dette tilbys til spotpris uten påslag. Fastprisen varierer for hvor mange år kunden ønsker å binde seg. Fleksikraft tilbys alle kunder av Ål Kraftverk KF. 3. Ål Kraftverk – Vinter - Inntil 80 % av forventa årsforbruk med fast profil gjennom året. Avtalen gjelder fra 1. november til 30. april. For neste periode er prisen på 161,2 øre/KWh. For forbruket utover fastprisen gjelder spotpris uten påslag. 4. Ål Kraftverk KF har også en kundegruppe som mottar gratis kraft. Dette som en del av konsesjonsvilkår for Holsutbyggingen og kalles Votnakraft. Dette forbruket er på ca. 4,4 GWh og det er tale om ca. 250 anlegg. Se nærmere om kravene til leveransen som skal tilbys Ål Kraftverk KFs kunder under punkt 2. Kontraktene reguleres av kontraktsvilkårene som er vedlagt konkurransegrunnlaget og spesifikasjonene som kommer frem i konkurransegrunnlaget. 1.3 Anbudskonkurransen vektlegger ikke klima- og miljøhensyn Etter anskaffelsesloven § 5b fremgår det i annet ledd at en «oppdragsgiver skal vekte klima- og miljøhensyn med minimum tretti prosent». Det vil i denne anbudskonkurransen likevel ikke legges vekt på klima- og miljøhensyn da anskaffelsen har et «uvesentlig klimaavtrykk», jf. anskaffelsesloven § 5b tredje ledd. Tjenesten Ål Kraftverk KF anskaffer omhandler håndteringen av kjøp av kraft og videreformidling av Ål Kraftverks sluttbrukerkunder. Det er tale om menneskelige ressurser i form av arbeidsinnsats som kjøpes, der klimaavtrykket og miljøbelastningen ligger utenfor hva som kan knyttes til anskaffelsens art jf. Direktoratet for forvaltning og økonomistyring (DFØ) sin veileder om klima og miljøhensyn i offentlige anskaffelser. Kommunen er dermed unntatt forpliktelsene om å evaluere på klima og miljø. NB! Se vedlagte konkurransegrunnlag

title: Spain – Hotel accommodation services – concesión del servicio de explotación del Hotel Oromana (C-2026/032)
description: El objeto del presente contrato es la concesión del servicio de explotación del Hotel Oromana, de titularidad municipal, situado en el municipio de Alcalá de Guadaíra, que comprende la gestión integral del establecimiento, así como la ejecución de las actuaciones necesarias de rehabilitación, reforma, posible ampliación y adecuación del inmueble para su correcto funcionamiento y mejora de categoría, todo ello conforme a lo establecido en el correspondiente pliego de prescripciones técnicas. La presente contratación tiene como finalidad la transformación integral del establecimiento hotelero, con el objetivo de su adecuación a los estándares actuales del sector y su posicionamiento como hotel de cuatro estrellas, mediante la ejecución de las actuaciones constructivas necesarias y la implantación de un modelo de gestión profesionalizado, eficiente y orientado a la calidad. No se pretende con esta licitación una mera explotación del establecimiento en su estado actual, sino la definición y desarrollo de un proyecto global y coherente que integre la intervención sobre el inmueble con un modelo de gestión hotelera alineado con el valor patrimonial, paisajístico y turístico del entorno en el que se inserta, contribuyendo a reforzar la identidad y singularidad del destino. En este sentido, la concesión deberá orientarse a la creación de una oferta hotelera de calidad, capaz de atraer tanto a visitantes como a usuarios locales, generando actividad económica, empleo y sinergias con otros sectores vinculados al turismo, la cultura y la hostelería, y actuando como elemento dinamizador del municipio y su entorno. Asimismo, el contrato comprende tanto la ejecución de las obras definidas como obligatorias, como, en su caso, la incorporación de mejoras propuestas por los licitadores, así como la gestión integral del establecimiento, incluyendo todos los servicios necesarios para su correcto funcionamiento. El detalle y alcance de todas estas prestaciones se desarrollan en el pliego de prescripciones técnicas que rige la presente contratación.

description: Technische Hochschule Mannheim, 68163 Mannheim, Paul-Wittsack-Str. 6, Gebäude G (alt), Gesamtsanierung Laborgebäude Ingenieurleistungen der Tragwerksplanung nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 1 HOAI, Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 1 bis 6 sowie Besondere Leistungen der Leistungsphasen 1, 3, 4 und 8. Das Land Baden-Württemberg, vertreten durch Vermögen und Bau Baden-Württemberg, beabsichtigt die Generalsanierung des Gebäudes G (Altbau) der Technischen Hochschule Mannheim. Das Gebäude G (Altbau) der Technischen Hochschule Mannheim wurde in den Jahren 1970 bis 1972 errichtet und dient als Labor- und Hörsaalgebäude. Aufgrund der langen Nutzungszeit von über 50 Jahren entspricht das Gebäude in baulicher, brandschutztechnischer und haustechnischer Hinsicht nicht mehr dem heutigen Stand der Technik, daher soll es generalsaniert werden. Es handelt sich um einen zweigeschossigen Stahlbetonskelettbau mit Untergeschoss und einer Nutzfläche von 1.473 m². Es beinhaltet bisher auf beiden Geschossen Laborbereiche (Kategorie S1) mit einer großen Anzahl von Digestorien und einen sich über das UG und EG erstreckenden innenliegenden Hörsaal mit ansteigendem Gestühl, im Bestand derzeit ohne natürliche Belichtung. Das Gebäude hat eine Grundfläche von 26,10m x 39,90m. Die Flächen der Generalsanierung belaufen sich auf 1.473 m² NUF R, die Gesamtfläche mit Verkehrs- und Technikflächen beläuft sich auf 2.929 m² NRF. Die Nutzung als Labor- und Hörsaalgebäude bleibt auch für die Zukunft erhalten. Die Generalsanierung beinhaltet den Rückbau des Gebäudes bis auf die statische Konstruktion. Die bisherige Stahlbetonfertigteilfassade wird demontiert - hier ist in gestalterischer und energetischer Hinsicht eine komplett neue Fassade gewünscht. Moderne Lernformen sind bei der Neukonzeption zu berücksichtigen und zu ermöglichen, etwa Lernflächen in den Flurzonen oder Projektgruppen-Arbeitsräume. Bisher fehlende Funktionsräume wie z. B. Umkleiden für die Labore oder barrierefreie WC-Anlagen sind zu ergänzen. Die geschätzten Bauwerkskosten sind ca. 19,3 Mio. €, für die KG 300 wird von 8,1 Mio. € und für die KG 400 von 11,2 Mio. € ausgegangen. Die bauzeitliche, geprüfte Statik von 1969 inkl. Nachträgen liegt vor, eine repräsentative Bestandsaufnahme und Bewertung tragender Bauteile ist dennoch notwendig. Der Baubeginn ist für Ende 2030 geplant, die Baufertigstellung für Ende 2033.

title: Sweden – Health services – SPR/260834 - Provision of genomic epidemiology and public health bioinformatics training
description: The overall objective of this tender is to procure a Framework Contract to strengthen the capacity for genomic epidemiology and public health bioinformatics through interdisciplinary trainings, which is crucial for response during a pandemic or unexpected major public health events. The general objectives of the trainings are to support countries in building up their capacity in genomic epidemiology and bioinformatics for public health purposes, and to increase the interdisciplinary collaboration between bioinformaticians, epidemiologists and microbiologists within a country to facilitate the routine use of genomic information for surveillance, preparedness, and outbreak response. Activities shall also enhance data sharing and collaborations between public health institutions and ECDC, and enhanced networking activities will foster cross-border collaborations. The target groups for the trainings are professionals working in public health institutions with a background in computational biology and bioinformatics; and professionals working in public health institutions who do not have a specific background in bioinformatics. The aims of the trainings are: * To allow the professionals with a background in computational biology and bioinformatics to: - enhance and extend their skills in order to strengthen their capacity in the field of public health bioinformatics; - better understand the needs and concepts of epidemiology and public health microbiology, with a focus on the inputs and outputs needed by their counterparts (i.e. microbiologists, epidemiologists, professionals in public health surveillance and response) to take rapid and informed public health action. * To allow the professionals without a background in computational biology/bioinformatics to: - gain a better understanding of how genomic epidemiology can be applied in a public health context with special focus on how traditional and genomic data can be jointly analysed, interpreted and used for public health purposes; - become more familiar with the concepts, formats and conventions commonly used in microbial genomics, and get a better understanding of how the structure and format of the data can be used to streamline the data analysis process; - better understand the concepts behind and use of the most common bioinformatic tools and pipelines used for epidemiological analyses, including limitations and possible alternatives; and - gain a better overview of the basic principles, options for and best practices of data storage, management and sharing, with a specific focus on sequencing data and associated metadata.

title: Germany – Vocational training services – 10018858-Implementation of TVET support and women's economic empowerment activities in Sierra Leone
description: Sierra Leone faces persistent poverty, high informality and limited job creation, disproportionately affecting women and youth. Agriculture is the largest employer, yet value chains are fragmented, processing is weak, and access to finance, quality infrastructure and certification is limited. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system suffers from outdated curricula, insufficient equipment and low private sector engagement, constraining labour market relevance, especially for women and returnees. The "Youth Employment Promotion through Socio Ecological and Economic Transformation of selected rural Value Chains" (EET project), commissioned by BMZ with EU co funding, supports inclusive, market oriented growth and better employment along selected value chains (cassava, coffee/cocoa, vegetables, poultry). It strengthens micro, small and medium sized enterprises (MSMEs) and the enabling ecosystem, with a strong focus on Women's Economic Empowerment (WEE) and youth integration. The project applies a concise multi level approach: support MSMEs with training, coaching and finance to improve productivity and market access; strengthen ecosystem actors (finance, certification, cooperatives, processing centres) to enhance services and linkages; and upgrade TVET through demand driven Competence Based Education and Training (CBET) curricula, improved facilities at Government Technical Institutes (GTIs) in Kabala, Kailahun, Koidu and Mattru Jong, teacher capacity building and institutionalised private sector engagement for apprenticeships and certification via Industry Sector Advisory Committees. WEE is embedded throughout. The project strengthens six representative bodies advancing women's economic rights (e.g. Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment - GEWE - Act), introduces gender transformative modules (Gender makes Business Sense - GmBS; Gender Action Learning Systems - GALS; Gender Model Family - GMF) via public and private providers, and delivers mentoring and awareness campaigns to address norms and improve women"s access to resources, markets and decision making. Outcomes are tracked with recognised tools such as the (pro )Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (pro WEAI). Key results targeted include: - Improved competitiveness of MSMEs with measurable employment effects for women and youth. - Upgraded GTIs and at least nine demand oriented, gender responsive curricula operational; teachers trained in learner centred CBET; trainees certified in line with National Council for Technical and Vocational Education (NCTVE) standards in the initial phase. - Stronger institutional conditions for women's economic participation, including operational representative bodies, integrated gender transformative modules, and functioning mentoring and communication platforms. - Enhanced market access through strengthened outgrower networks, cooperative services and business linkages, enabling more equitable participation of women and young producers. The approach is rights based, conflict and context sensitive, and climate aware. It promotes green and circular economy elements in training and enterprise support, limits environmental footprints and applies Do No Harm principles. Implementation aligns with national policies (TVET Policy, Dual Apprenticeship Policy) under the coordination of the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development, with the Ministry of Technical and Higher Education (MTHE) and NCTVE responsible for TVET standards and certification, and the Ministry of Gender and Children's Affairs and civil society partners advancing WEE. Continuous monitoring, learning and adaptive management ensure data driven steering and accountability to BMZ and the EU. EU visibility will follow EU visual identity guidelines; co branding with BMZ/GIZ will follow donor rules.?

description: Die gewählten städtischen Flächen zur Entwicklung eines Gesamtschulstandortes mit Gymnasialer Oberstufe bieten sich aufgrund der bereits vorhandenen Infrastruktur bestens an. Auf dem zur Verfügung stehenden Gelände befindet sich entlang der Joliot-Curie-Straße bereits ein Gebäuderiegel, der schon zu DDR- Zeiten eine Polytechnische Oberschule beherbergte und derzeit für die Schule des Zweiten Bildungsweges genutzt wird. Komplettiert wird der vorhandene Gebäudekomplex von einer kleinen Sporthalle, deren Errichtungszeitraum, wie bei den Schulgebäuden, in die Zeit zum Ende der 1960er Jahre einzuordnen ist. Aktuell nutzen Vereine die räumlichen Kapazitäten für ihren Trainingsbetrieb. Die genauen Angaben entnehmen Sie bitte der Leistungsbeschreibung.

The programme contributes to the implementation of the EU Pact for the Mediterranean and supports the regional Team Europe Initiative (TEI) "Jobs through Trade & Investment in the Southern Neighbourhood", promoting structured exchange among governments, regional organisations, the private sector, financial institutions and other stakeholders. While the programme focuses on UfM Member States in North Africa and the Middle East, EU Member States and the Western Balkans are actively involved in peer learning and the exchange of best practices. title: Germany – Financial and insurance services – 10045510-Consultancy support services for the development and implementation of sustainable finance taxonomies
description: The objective of GIZ's global project Sustainable Economic Transformation and Sustainable Finance is to advance the transformation towards a more sustainable economy and financial sector, grounded in international standards and global agendas. To this end, the project implements activities in three main areas of intervention: - Pillar 1: Fostering global knowledge exchange and peer-learning regarding the sustainable transformation of the economy and the financial sector. - Pillar 2: Supporting development of policy and regulatory frameworks in partner countries governing the transformation toward a sustainable economy and financial sector in partner countries. - Pillar 3: Providing advisory services and technical assistance to embed sustainability in governance and financial decision-making of financial institutions. In pillar 2, the project supports partner countries in aligning their financial regulatory and policy frameworks with international standards and best practices on sustainable finance. This encompasses, for example, the development of taxonomies, disclosure regulations, sustainable financial product standards or policies on ESG risk management. The project's activities include, for example, supporting the development of national taxonomies in Rwanda, Peru, Senegal, Ghana, The Philippines, and Mexico. The support provided by GIZ is comprehensive, including strategic advice, capacity building, design of multi-stakeholder processes (e.g., coordination of technical expert groups, support for public consultation), drafting advice (e.g., on the selection of sectors and screening criteria), and supporting the taxonomy's dissemination and implementation. This process is complemented by peer-learning opportunities and featuring lessons learned from implementation in partner countries in relevant international and regional forums. The objective of this tender is to establish a flexible pool of specialized technical expertise that can support sustainable finance taxonomy initiatives in partner countries designated by GIZ during the contract period. The contractor will provide advisory services covering the development, enhancement and implementation of sustainable finance taxonomies, as well as related analytical work, capacity building and knowledge products.

title: GOCO Industry Day
description: Executive Summary The current operating strategy for Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) Army ammunition plants requires reassessment to ensure the Organic Industrial Base can meet future requirements for safety, responsiveness, capacity, modernization, supply-chain resilience, and affordable lifecycle performance. Traditional GOCO competition and contract approaches may not consistently create the incentives, flexibility, or accountability necessary to operate Government-owned facilities as modern and competitive manufacturing enterprises. In particular, existing approaches may overemphasize Government-directed workload and reimbursed facility operations rather than operator responsibility for productive utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce development, workload capture, and operational performance. The Government is seeking industry input on a commercially disciplined GOCO operating model that preserves Government mission priorities while providing the operating contractor meaningful responsibility and flexibility to manage the facility as a competitive manufacturing enterprise. Under such a model, the contractor would be expected to sustain, modernize, maintain, and improve the facility through efficient operations, productive utilization, pursuit of approved workload, and sound business practices. The Government seeks to identify contracting, workload, risk-allocation, facility-use, oversight, intellectual-property, and performance-management constructs that will enable this model while preserving appropriate Government accountability, safety, security, and access to required production capacity. Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE AS&A) is assessing the future GOCO operating strategy before proceeding with future GOCO competitions. Purpose Army Contracting Command � Rock Island, on behalf of PAE AS&A, intends to host an Industry Day in November 2026 focused on transforming the operating strategy for GOCO Army ammunition plants. Specific Industry Day details will be provided separately; registration is not currently required. This Request for Information (RFI), together with the subsequent Industry Day, will help the Government understand feasible business and operating models for future GOCO facilities. The Government will use industry feedback to inform discussion of alternative approaches to facility operations, modernization, workload management, contract structure, and oversight. Objective The Government�s objective is to establish a commercially disciplined operating model for GOCO Army ammunition plants that improves responsiveness to Warfighter requirements while sustaining long-term plant viability, modernization, competitiveness, and accountability. The desired model would provide the operating contractor with appropriate flexibility and meaningful responsibility to manage facility utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce, supply chain, and approved workload. The Government seeks input on the risk-allocation mechanisms, workload authorities, facility-use structures, performance measures, and oversight approaches necessary to support this model while preserving Government mission priorities. The desired end state is a modern, flexible production enterprise capable of efficiently increasing, reducing, pausing, restarting, changing over, and surging production in response to Warfighter need without disproportionate impacts to cost, schedule, quality, workforce readiness, safety, or production capability. The Government is particularly interested in performance measures that demonstrate: Safe and reliable operations; Schedule reliability and order-to-delivery responsiveness; Plant availability and production throughput; Rapid changeover, shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Flexible, modular, dual-use, and/or automated manufacturing capacity; Effective maintenance, workforce, and supply-chain management; Competitive lifecycle cost and productive utilization; Modernization outcomes that improve operating performance; and Appropriate transparency and accountability without unnecessary Government direction of day-to-day operations. Areas of Consideration The Government developed the attached questionnaire based on the following interconnected areas of consideration. Respondents are requested to complete the associated questionnaire and provide practical recommendations, examples, and lessons learned from relevant commercial, defense-industrial, or other manufacturing environments. Commercial Operating Model and Risk Allocation The Government seeks input on operating models in which the contractor manages a Government-owned facility with commercial discipline while meeting Government mission priorities. These reports will include summaries of patient characteristics, facility characteristics, patient outcomes, and facility practice patterns. These reports will include comparative state, network, regional, and national statistics as appropriate. These reports will be used by CMS in overseeing the quality and safety of the ESRD, Transplant and OPO Programs. For the Dialysis Facility Reports (DFRs), the contractor will use data from a variety of sources to create summary reports to be used to provide Federal, state and facility oversight of dialysis facilities. Data from all available sources, including the CMS Central Data Repository (CDR), claims forms, eligibility forms, clinical data sources, facility inventories, death forms, and survey and certification forms will be updated, edited, validated, and utilized by the contractor to create a series of reports that will assist CMS, states, and other entities in monitoring the care provided by ESRD facilities. These reports will be risk-adjusted and facility, state, regional, and corporate-specific for each fiscal year. The reports shall include a rank-ordered Outcomes List of ESRD facilities for each state. The Outcomes Lists will be constructed from a composite of data elements that most validly and reliably identify facilities with potential problems. The contractor will routinely revise the DFRs to ensure they are 1) aligned with the ESRD Survey process, 2) provide development of data sources and data tools to allow state surveyors convenient and timely access to more current dialysis facility quality outcomes, 3) use state surveyor and other DFR user feedback to determine the need for revisions. The contractor will provide guidance on using advanced technologies and incorporate plans to integrate emerging technologies associated with Electronic Health Records (EHRs). The contractor will prepare Transplant Program reports and OPO reports. The data for these reports will be obtained from the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) of the Health Resources and Services Agency (HRSA), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and Multiple Cause of Death (MCOD) databases. Scope of Work: The scope of work shall generally consist of, but not limited to the following: The project involves upgrading the Hot Water Heater system (specifically Buildings 3, 7, 53, 54, and 143 and their associated mechanical and utility spaces). The existing domestic hot water heating systems at the Lyons VA Medical Center consist of aging tank type and semi-instantaneous water heaters and associated recirculation pumps that are inefficient, and beyond their intended service life. These units serve critical patient care, residential, and support areas and must be upgraded to meet current VA design standards, energy efficiency requirements, and plumbing and electrical codes while maintaining continuous hot water service to the occupied facility. The water heaters shall be replaced sequentially so that only one unit is taken out of service at a given time, and the others remain in full operation. This approach will ensure continuous domestic hot water service to the building throughout construction, with at least one operational hot water heater. Replacing these units will significantly reduce maintenance time, improve system control and enhance the distribution of hot water across rooms, floors, and departments. The contractor shall completely prepare site for building operations, including demolishing selected existing water heaters, recirculation pumps, and associated steam, condensate, and domestic water piping and furnish and install new semi-instantaneous steam to hot water heaters, recirculation pumps, condensate receiver/pump, piping, insulation, electrical feeders, disconnects, and controls as indicated in the 100% construction documents. Work also includes startup, testing, balancing, commissioning and training the VA plumbing staff on the new equipment. The contractor shall also furnish all labor, materials, tool, and supervision necessary to perform work for VA Project 561A4-23-101 Replace Multiple Building s Water Heaters, in accordance with AE drawings and specifications. title: Canada – Public relations services – Policy Dialogue and Public Diplomacy Facility for Canada
description: The purpose of this procurement is to procure services that strengthen and deepen EU–Canada relations on key priority themes of shared strategic interest, while advancing EU interests and values in Canada through targeted policy dialogue and public diplomacy. The contract will support the implementation of commitments under the EU–Canada Strategic Partnership Agreement (SPA), the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), and, where relevant, other bilateral frameworks including the EU–Canada Green Alliance and the EU–Canada Security and Defence Partnership. The procured services shall comprise two complementary components: Policy Dialogue Support — facilitation of structured policy dialogues across a wide range of areas through concrete activities linked to existing and emerging dialogue mechanisms, including joint committees and working groups involving the EU Delegation and relevant EU services. Public Diplomacy Actions — Design and delivery of public diplomacy initiatives aimed at increasing understanding of EU policies and priorities among Canadian audiences, demonstrating the tangible benefits of the EU–Canada partnership, and strengthening engagement with key Canadian stakeholders beyond government — including media, academia, civil society, youth, and opinion leaders. The services shall deliver measurable policy outcomes, consolidate trusted stakeholder networks, and amplify EU positions across Canada. Through the combined effect of policy dialogue and public diplomacy, the procurement aims to enhance the visibility and credibility of the EU in Canada and contribute to closer alignment between EU and Canadian policy positions and approaches, including in multilateral fora, on major foreign policy priorities.

title: CFA-686 Carbon-based Fuels Capability - CO2 Storage Vessel
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to support the design, fabrication, testing, and inspection of a pressure vessel for the Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability. PROCESS BEA is seeking qualified firms to compete for the design/build contract in support of the CFA-686 CO2 Storage Vessel (V-738). As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that will require detailed technical and price proposals be provided for evaluation and ranking under a source selection process. Interested firms are advised that RFP release and the source selection/award decision timeline will be communicated following review of submitted EOIs. The contract award type will be firm?fixed price. The total anticipated duration for completion of all work is 28 weeks ARO, and the estimated sequential schedule is as follows: ASME Code design and analysis (3 weeks), shop fabrication drawings (4 weeks), WPS/PQR submittal and approval (3 weeks), complete shop fabrication including cleaning (25 weeks), install heating elements and insulate vessel (26 weeks), ship vessel to INL (27 weeks), and submission of the final Code Data Report, as?built drawings, and all other deliverables (28 weeks). PROJECT DESCRIPTION The vessel will be designed, fabricated, inspected, and delivered for the INL Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability (CFA-686). The vessel, designated V-738, is a 200 cubic foot ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 code "U" stamped pressure vessel for gaseous CO2 service, with a design pressure of 1,800 psig and a design temperature range of -40�F to 500�F. The vessel is a horizontal configuration with two saddle supports spaced 16 feet apart, a 36-inch inner diameter, minimum 2-inch shell thickness, minimum 1-inch hemispherical head thickness, and an overall shell length of 26 feet 3-1/2 inches. The vessel includes seven nozzles (inlet, outlet, five inspection ports, a low point drain, a pressure relief nozzle, and two instrumentation ports), nine band heating elements (3.6 kW total) to maintain the vessel above 150�F, and Foamglas (or equivalent) insulation with protective aluminum sheathing. The vessel will be installed outdoors at INL in a high desert environment, with an altitude of 4,900 ft, ambient temperatures ranging from -40�F to 100�F, and exposure to wind, blowing sand, dust, snow, and frost. The vessel must be designed for static, seismic, and wind loading in accordance with IBC 2024, ASCE 7-10, and ACI 318-19, and fabricated from 304/304L stainless steel pressure boundary materials. Specific fabrication drawings, foundation details, and design calculations will be provided to qualified offerors as part of the RFP process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest to Chase Egbert (chase.egbert@inl.gov) by close-of-business on 10/16/2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder's qualifications addressing each of the following criteria: Experience in ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 pressure vessel design and fabrication, including possession of a current "U" stamp certificate for both design and fabrication. Experience with stainless steel pressure vessel welding, including full penetration butt welds, 100% radiography, and carbide precipitation control during welding. Capability to meet the design/build schedule outlined above. Capability to fabricate the vessel in the required configuration, including nozzle arrangement, saddle supports, band heating elements, and insulation system. Proper identification and execution plan for inspection, examination, and testing, including hydrostatic testing, positive material identification, liquid penetrant testing, and radiography or phased array ultrasonic testing. Agreement to maintain a written Quality Control System consistent with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 10. Compliance with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 47 requirements for pressure vessel design. Availability of a qualified and experienced project manager and Quality Control Manager to oversee the work. Note that responses must be no more than 5 pages in length. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will receive the RFP for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in November 2026. title: CFA-686 Carbon-based Fuels Capability CO2 Compressor Design/Build
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to support the design, fabrication, testing, and delivery of a CO2 compressor for the Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability. PROCESS BEA is seeking qualified firms to compete for the design/build contract in support of the CFA-686 CO2 Compressor. As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that will require detailed technical and price proposals be provided for evaluation and ranking under a source selection process. Interested firms are advised that RFP release and the source selection/award decision timeline will be communicated following review of submitted EOIs. The contract award type will be firm-fixed price. Per the proposed project schedule, all durations are After Receipt of Order (ARO): Engineering Documentation Report (3 weeks), shop fabrication drawings (4 weeks), complete shop fabrication (40 weeks), and compressor arrival at INL (3 weeks). PROJECT DESCRIPTION The compressor will be designed, fabricated, tested, and delivered for the INL Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability (CFA-686). The compressor will be used to compress CO2 from a combustor unit into a storage vessel that will supply gas to downstream users, and will be housed in a protected shipping container. The compressor shall be oil-free, liquid-cooled, fixed speed, and electric motor driven. Inlet conditions are 50-100�F at 0.14-2 psig; outlet conditions are 1,400 psig, 66.1 scfm, and 150�F, with the unit operating on a nearly continuous basis. The compressor and all components must fit within a high cube shipping container with interior dimensions of 19'6" long x 7'9" wide x 8'10" high, and must be mounted on a structural frame designed and fabricated in accordance with the American Institute of Steel Construction (AISC), with welding per AWS D1.1. Any pressure vessels used in fabrication of the compressor must be designed and fabricated in accordance with ASME Section VIII, Division 1, and stamped and registered with the National Board. The compressor must withstand a CO2 gas stream composition of approximately 99% CO2 with trace nitrogen, oxygen, water vapor, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, sulfur oxides, hydrocarbons, hydrogen sulfide, and hydrogen chloride. The unit will be installed at INL at an altitude of approximately 4,938 ft, with a shipping container temperature range of 41�F to 104�F and humidity from 0 to 100%. The compressor package must include a control panel with instrumentation and alarms for conditions such as low discharge pressure and motor failure, a data history logging function, an emergency shutoff switch, and UL-508A listed control panels. The unit must be provided with inter-coolers or after-coolers to maintain outlet temperature at or below 150�F, and a stainless steel drip pan sized to contain at least 1.5 times the volume of any fluids contained in the compressor. Specific fabrication drawings, nozzle location diagrams, and design details will be provided to qualified offerors as part of the RFP process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest to Chase Egbert (chase.egbert@inl.gov) by close-of-business on 10/16/2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder's qualifications addressing each of the following criteria: Experience in design and fabrication of oil-free, liquid-cooled CO2 or industrial gas compressor packages. Experience with ASME Section VIII, Division 1 pressure vessel design where applicable to compressor components, and structural fabrication in accordance with AISC and AWS D1.1. Capability to meet the design/build schedule outlined above. Capability to package the compressor, motor, controls, and all interconnecting piping and instrumentation within the required shipping container footprint. Proper identification and execution plan for inspection, examination, and testing, including non-destructive examination of castings and welds, operational testing, and a 10-hour continuous reliability test. Agreement to maintain a written Quality Assurance Plan based on a national consensus code such as ANSI/ASME ISO-9000. Capability to provide Operations & Maintenance documentation, a Recommended Spare Parts List, and field support for startup and commissioning. Note that responses must be no more than 5 pages in length. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will receive the RFP for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in November 2026. The vessel must be designed for static, seismic, and wind loading in accordance with IBC 2024, ASCE 7-10, and ACI 318-19, and fabricated from 304/304L stainless steel pressure boundary materials. Capability to meet the design/build schedule outlined above. title: Justification for Other Than Full and Open - Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System � California
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awarded Contract No. 75D30126P21605 to the California Department of Public Health for the Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System � California. The requirement is for the identification and provision of California vital records necessary to support CDC's Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System. The California Department of Public Health is the sole legal custodian and authoritative source of the required California vital records. Market research confirmed that the required records are maintained exclusively by the State of California and are not available from other sources in the required format. The contract includes a 12-month Base Period and four 12-month Option Periods. The Base Period value is $10,074.43, and the total potential contract value, is $49,012.15. In accordance with RFO Part 6, the approved Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC) is being made publicly available with this notice. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. The contract has already been awarded, and the Government is not soliciting or accepting proposals in response to this notice. This notice is being published solely to provide public notice of the award and the associated Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC).

description: Предмет на настоящата обществена поръчка е доставка на специализирано лабораторно оборудване и консумативи за молекулярно-биологичен анализ, което да позволи на високо научно ниво да се дефинира влиянието на променливи фактори, обусловени от климатичните изменения, върху генетичния отговор на лозята, включително експресията на гени, свързани с устойчивост към биотичен и абиотичен стрес, както и ранно откриване на патогени (вируси, бактерии, фитоплазми и гъби) по лозата. Поръчката включва следните обособени позиции: Обособена позиция №1: „Доставка на консумативи за PCR и Real time PCR за текуща лабораторна работа“; Обособена позиция №2: „Доставка на ламинарни боксове (микробиологичен клас II А2 и за PCR) и лабораторна камина“; Обособена позиция № 3: „Доставка на общолабораторно оборудване“; Обособена позиция № 4: „Доставка на Автоклав“; Обособена позиция № 5: “Доставка на олигонуклеотиди (PCR праймери)”. ​​​​Дейността се финансира като част от проект „Адаптиране на лозарството към изменението на климата чрез прилагане на екосистемни мерки за поддържане на икономическата жизнеспособност (VitiClimRoBg–Hard ROBG00370)“, по Програма Interreg VI-A Румъния-България, специфична цел: 2.4 — Насърчаване на адаптирането към изменението на климата, предотвратяването на риска от бедствия и устойчивостта, като се вземат предвид екосистемни подходи. Специализираното оборудване, обект на настоящата обществена поръчка, е в интеграция с предходно заявени компоненти по проекта, за да се постигне интегриран комплексен подход, пряко обвързан с адаптацията към климатичните изменения. Целта е допълване на теренни и физикохимични данни с молекулярно-генетичен анализ, предоставящ прецизни, възпроизводими и научно обосновани резултати, които да очертаят връзката на климатичните изменения с генетичните механизми на адаптация на лозята, генерирайки последователно прилагане на устойчиви практики за „борба“ с климатичния отпечатък и установяване на икономическа жизнеспособност.

(UEI:RD55NEXJ5EW4 / CAGE:3K773) Joint Base Andrews has a requirement to procure, install, and integrate a comprehensive Security Management System for a specific facility. Major items include high-definition cameras, PIV-class card readers, Servers, Server Software and Licenses. The required components and service for integration in the current proprietary intrusion detection system are provided by M.C. Dean Inc. Air Force physical security standards and Integrated Base Defense Security System (IBDSS) guidelines mandate that all electronic security systems, intrusion detection systems, and access control platforms maintain strict Department of Defense (DoD) Joint Services Interior Security Commission (JSIDS) and USAF Protection Level 1 (PL-1) non-nuclear security certifications. Only items fully certified and compatible with the existing base head-end software and network backbone are authorized for installation and integration. While competition for various security requirements exist, market research conducted by the Government revealed only one responsible vendor would be able to support this effort due to the vital, pre-established integrated security functions and nature of facility operations. In addition to sensitive operations at Joint Base Andrews, site surveys were limited to approved GSA vendors to minimize risk while protecting critical national security information. The government will continue to monitor the updated Air Force certified equipment lists for all future purchases of this nature to verify if competition is available to include sourcing potential Governmentwide acquisition contracts and other approved vehicles. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. This notice is for informational purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the government. Vendors that believe they can provide the items listed above are invited to submit substantiating documentation in writing to the identified point of contact. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. A determination by the government to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the government.

title: Systems for Phenotypic Evaluation, Clinical Trajectories, Response, and Agency (SPECTRA)
description: SPECTRA will identify and act on autism trajectories, the evolving developmental paths individuals follow across the lifespan from the prenatal period through aging, spanning autism characteristics, co-occurring conditions, and functional outcomes together with the genetic, biological, behavioral, iatrogenic (medical influences), environmental factors and their nonlinear interactions. Rather than examining these factors in isolation, SPECTRA will examine how they combine and interact, including their nonlinear interactions, to produce autism and its co-occurring conditions over time. SPECTRA will also develop technologies that serve two purposes at once: extending reliable assessment beyond the clinic while improving everyday communication, function, and quality of life. The same tools people use to live more fully will also generate the data that drive measurement and personalized care.

title: Independent Evaluation of the Better Security, Better Care Programme (October 2025 to October 2028)
description: Digital Care Hub is seeking an independent evaluation partner to assess the delivery, impact, sustainability and value for money of the Better Security, Better Care (BSBC) programme. Funded by the Department of Health and Social Care, BSBC supports approximately 28,000 CQC-registered adult social care locations in England to improve cyber security, data protection and information governance, including compliance with the Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT). Delivery is led nationally by Digital Care Hub through more than 30 Local Support Organisations, combining central leadership, guidance, training, communications, data analysis and performance management with trusted local support. The supplier will design and deliver a proportionate mixed-method evaluation covering programme governance and delivery, stakeholder engagement, partner effectiveness, reach, changes in awareness and behaviour, adoption of good practice, DSPT outcomes, organisational resilience, wider benefits, cost effectiveness, return on investment and social and economic value. The work should identify lessons, good practice and evidence-based recommendations while providing ongoing insight to support continuous improvement. Key deliverables are an evaluation framework and inception report within three months; ongoing data collection, analysis and stakeholder engagement; monthly progress meetings; an interim report by September 2027; and a final evaluation report, shorter executive report, presentation and dissemination-ready outputs by October 2028. Close-down and dissemination support will continue to March 2029. The proposed contract runs from October 2026 to March 2029, with a maximum budget of £125,000 inclusive of VAT. Bidders must demonstrate strong experience in programme and economic evaluation, publicly funded programmes, mixed-method research, stakeholder engagement and report writing. Knowledge of adult social care, health and care systems, cyber security, digital transformation or information governance is required. Tender responses must include organisation and personnel details, methodology, data collection and analysis plans, delivery timetable, resourcing, quality assurance, risk management, up to three relevant examples, a full pricing schedule, assumptions and proposed social value. Evaluation weightings are: understanding 15%, methodology 35%, experience 20%, project management 10%, social value 10% and price 10%. The supplier must comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, confidentiality, insurance, procurement, equality and safeguarding requirements. Clarification questions are due by 14 October 2026 and tenders by 18 October 2026. Please see attachment for full specifications.
